quote: MFuser enhances feature locality while leveraging domain-invariant semantic knowledge provided by text embeddings to effectively constrain visual representations.

quote: The overall framework of our proposed SCSD is depicted in Fig. 3, consisting of three key components: Semantic Query Booster (SQB), Text-Driven Style Transform (TDST), and Style Synergy Optimization (SSO).

quote: To efficiently fine-tune VFMs, spectral-decomposed tokens are applied to each frozen layer. Within each layer, the frozen features are decomposed into amplitude and phase components by Fast Fourier Transform (FFT).
claim: The SET method applies spectral-decomposed tokens to frozen VFM layers, decomposing features into amplitude and phase components via FFT.

quote: the phase component, which contains more low-frequency component on the scene content, is relatively stable despite the cross-style variation. In contrast, the amplitude component, which has more high-frequency component on the styles, can be rather unstable when handling images from different domains.
claim: The key insight is that phase components contain stable content information while amplitude components capture style variations across domains.

quote: The proposed SET shows an mIoU improvement of 1.66%, 1.24%, 1.58% and 1.15% on C, B, M and S unseen target domains, respectively, compared to the VFM based state-of-the-art Rein.

quote: our method leverages the feature information through two main approaches: covariance alignment and semantic consistency contrastive learning. Specifically, the covariance matching ensures that features, having different styles but the same content, contain similar information.

quote: While these approaches effectively remove style-related information, they simultaneously pose the challenge of removing semantic content because content and style information are entangled.
claim: Existing feature normalization methods struggle because removing style information also removes entangled semantic content.

quote: Our method outperforms all other methods when trained on GTAV, using ResNet-50 as the backbone. When compared with FN methods that remove domain-specific styles, we demonstrate that our approach minimizes the loss of content information.
claim: BlindNet outperforms all other DGSS methods on GTAV training and minimizes content information loss compared to feature normalization methods.

quote: The key idea of our method is to utilize text embeddings of classes of interest from VLMs as object queries, referred to as textual object queries. Given that an object query can be considered as a mask embedding vector to group regions belonging to the same class, textual object queries generate robust mask predictions for classes of interest across diverse domains, thanks to their domain-invariant semantics.
claim: tqdm uses text embeddings from VLMs as textual object queries that provide domain-invariant semantics for robust mask predictions across diverse domains.

quote: Our tqdm demonstrates the state-of-the-art performance across multiple DGSS benchmarks; e.g., tqdm achieves 68.9 mIoU on GTA5 → Cityscapes, which improves the prior state-of-the-art method by 2.5 mIoU.
claim: tqdm achieves state-of-the-art 68.9 mIoU on GTA5→Cityscapes, improving the prior best method by 2.5 mIoU.

quote: To maintain this alignment, we propose three regularization strategies: (1) language regularization that prevents the learnable prompts from distorting the semantic meaning of text embeddings, (2) vision-language regularization that ensures the pixel-level alignment between visual and textual features, and (3) vision regularization that preserves the textual alignment capability of the vision encoder from a pre-trained VLM.
claim: tqdm employs three regularization losses to maintain vision-language alignment: language regularization, vision-language regularization, and vision regularization.

quote: While ControlNet effectively integrates condition masks into the generation process, it struggles with generating small objects due to the low-resolution latent space. claim: DGInStyle addresses ControlNet's limitation with small objects through a two-stage Multi-Resolution Latent Fusion pipeline.

claim: Rein employs learnable tokens that are randomly initialized and embedded with knowledge from the fine-tuning dataset to bridge the gap between pre-training and target scenes.

quote: The idea is to mine proxy domains and explore intermediate ones in a class-aware manner (as detailed in Sec. 3.3), which makes our work fundamentally different from [11], that steers features towards a particular target style and corresponding domain, and better suited to generalization.
claim: FAMix mines class-specific style banks using random prompts to explore intermediate proxy domains in a class-aware manner, which is fundamentally different from steering towards a particular target domain.

claim: FAMix significantly outperforms all baseline DGSS methods across all target datasets for both ResNet-50 and ResNet-101 backbones in single-source DGSS setting.

quote: By utilizing UDA techniques, we overcome the semantic inconsistency limitation of diffusion models, ensuring improved domain generalization performance.

claim: DIDEX outperforms state-of-the-art domain generalization methods by a large margin on common benchmarks.

section: 3.2 Preserving Style Prior with Style Swap
quote: As a first step of our Style Swap technique, we fine-tune the base LDM's U-Net \mathbf{U}^{\mathcal{P}} encapsulating the prior domain \mathcal{P} with the Dreambooth protocol [53] using all images in the source domain \mathcal{S} . The resulting U-Net is denoted as \mathbf{U}^{\mathcal{S}} . Second, we use \mathbf{U}^{\mathcal{S}} as the base model instead of \mathbf{U}^{\mathcal{P}} to initialize ControlNet.
claim: DGInStyle's Style Swap technique fine-tunes LDM with DreamBooth, trains ControlNet on the style-adapted model, then swaps back to original LDM for inference to preserve style diversity.

quote: We present a robust fine-tuning method, namely "Rein", to parameter-efficiently harness VFMs.
claim: The key contribution of paper 2312.04265 is Rein, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method for VFMs.

quote: In this work, we propose a novel method that tackles the domain generalization problem by diffusion-based domain extension (DIDEX).
claim: Paper 2312.01850 proposes DIDEX, a diffusion-based domain extension method for domain generalization.

quote: Overview: CLOUDS uses a CNN-based CLIP backbone, harnessing its capability to extract robust features (Section 3.1).
claim: CLOUDS uses a CNN-based CLIP backbone to extract robust features for domain generalized semantic segmentation.

quote: Lastly, the predicted pseudo labels are refined with the help of the Segment-Anything Model (SAM) in a student-teacher fashion (Section 3.3).
claim: CLOUDS refines pseudo labels using SAM in a student-teacher fashion to improve generalizability.
